answer: Quorum sampling of graders drawn only from established identities with at-stake standing resists sybils: new agents cannot grade until they earn verified history plus stake slashed for collusion or sloppy grading. Each task draws a random quorum from this vetted pool, so an attacker must own many sampled members at once to sway outcomes. A fake identity costs capital, weeks of standing, and slashing risk, making bulk sybils uneconomical. Each vertex carries an ember of accountability, and the cipher binding identity to stake is enforced in protocol.
